title: Unique items, sorted
description: Write a function `unique_items(items)` that returns a sorted list of the unique values found in the list `items`, with duplicates removed.
hints: There is a built-in collection type designed specifically to hold only unique values.
Passing `items` to `set()` removes duplicates, and `sorted()` turns any iterable into an ordered list.
Convert `items` to a set with `set(items)` to drop duplicates, then wrap that in `sorted(...)` to get a deterministic list.
expected_behavior: Returns a list containing each distinct value from `items`, sorted in ascending order.
explanation: `set(items)` builds a set from the list, which automatically discards duplicate values since sets only store unique elements. `sorted()` then converts that set into a list in ascending order, giving a deterministic, duplicate-free result.
